clause: DESIGN R3.3 §9.4 Region geometry, including Process IO
witness: object centres stay on one line when label heights differ (no per-stack centring)
derivation: Two 36000x50000 objects with labels 30000x14000 and 30000x28000, tokens 30000/10000/20000/60000, anchors centred at 230000 and 490000: lefts 212000, 472000; RH = max(60000, 78000 + 20000) = 98000; A = 25000, B = max(39000, 53000) = 53000, cy = max(25000, (98000 + 25000 - 53000)/2) = 35000: both objects at y 10000 and both labels at y 60000 (a per-stack centring would put the first object at y 17000, centre 42000, off the row line; DESIGN §9.4 'align centers on one IO row'). Row rule (spec §4.3): items in §7.2 placement order; footprint max(object, label) width; left = anchor centre - footprint/2 when the anchor is shown, else contentLeft or previous right + gap; clamp to contentLeft; collision shifts right; one row at the top of the support body [Ly, Ly+RH], RH = max(minHeight, max(object+label) + 2 padding) (harmonization K2); every object centre lies on one line cy = Ly + max(A, (RH + A - B)/2), A = max h/2, B = max(h/2 + label height), so the union of the stacks is centred in the row (DESIGN §9.4 'align centers on one IO row'); exact rationals, one roundEven per output coordinate.
